kinds.d: Pheasant sold whole or as any cut, wild-shot or farm-reared.

x.d: The pheasant reared and released in great numbers for shooting in Britain and Europe; hen birds are preferred for roasting.
x.dt: hen or cock · wild-shot or farmed · UK season from 1 October

kinds.d: Grouse sold whole or as any cut, wild-shot.

x.d: Moorland grouse of Britain whose season opens on the Glorious Twelfth (12 August).
x.dt: young or old bird · season from 12 August

x.d: Larger grouse, male called blackcock; a listed game bird but rarely shot as numbers decline.
Mountain grouse of the Highlands and the Arctic; a festive dish in Iceland.

kinds.d: Partridge sold whole or as any cut.

x.d: Partridge introduced to Britain from France in the 18th century, now reared and released for shooting.
Native European partridge, a popular game bird also introduced to North America.

kinds.d: Wild duck (mallard, teal, wigeon) sold whole or as any cut.

x.d: The commonest wild duck shot; breast and thigh are eaten, roasted or braised.
Small wild duck, a UK quarry species.

kinds.d: Wild wood pigeon or farmed young pigeon (squab) sold whole or as breasts.

x.d: Wild pigeon shot in millions as quarry and crop pest across Europe; leaner and tougher than squab.
Meat of a young domestic pigeon, usually about four weeks old.

kinds.d: Quail sold whole, spatchcocked or boned.

x.d: The farmed quail, raised worldwide for eggs and meat; meat strains reach about 300 g.
European quail, heavily hunted on migration and sometimes farmed.

kinds.d: Farmed guinea fowl sold whole or as any cut.

x.d: The domesticated guinea fowl species sold in Western supermarkets.
French free-range pintade fermière from a slow-growing breed, reared at least 94 days.
Guinea fowl raised on farms in the Bresse region of eastern France.

notes: All seven planned kinds kept; species are archetypes, season and wild/farmed are detail or types. Wigeon kept as a type (fetched page does not confirm it as food). Woodcock and snipe left out: no fetched page shows them sold. No brands (no maker archetypes).
